item.description:
Kento Alpha 0.9.34, build 2885

Speed

  • Colorspace works each pixel's color out once for its red, green and blue, where it had worked it out once for each channel. Comps with many Colorspace nodes, such as layers blended in their own color space, render faster: on one studio comp Colorspace took half the time.
  • FilterErode with the Box filter costs the same at any size. At large sizes it is many times faster: a size of 200 took about 2 seconds a frame and now takes a few hundredths. One studio comp's frame went from 5.1 to 2.9 seconds.
  • Both give exactly the same pixels as before, checked against every Write of five studio comps.

Kento Alpha 0.9.33, build 2872

Fixes

  • Playback draws each frame at the picture's own size. With a plate whose size differs from the comp's format, the playing frame was drawn smaller over the stopped one, a double image.
  • Every node's panel keeps to its grid. PlanarTracker's multipass switches ran off the panel's edge.
  • A menu shows its choice ticked when the knob holds another spelling of it: Transform's, Reformat's and CornerPin2D's filter showed "Cubic" as plain text, and PointsTo3D's camera type its "free move".
  • OCIODisplay's display and view list the comp's own color config. A name the config hasn't got, such as Nuke's "ACES", says which display or view is used in its place.
  • Write's frame mode and frame share one row, as Read's do.
  • A track that stops says where and why, on the Tracker panel and to an assistant through the remote control.

Nuke scripts

  • Gamma takes a value for each channel, as Nuke's does. Glow_Exponential's per-channel gammas were ignored.
  • Expressions with Nuke's | and & work, grouped as Nuke groups them, and && and || give 1 or 0 as in Nuke. Spill_Correct's switches were ignored.
  • Expressions can read another node's box, format and pixel aspect (Crop1.bbox.x), a group's own width (parent.width), $gui, and Nuke's obsolete knobs (read as 0, as Nuke reads them).
  • Card2's lattice comes in as written: every card in the studio's comps was reported as an expression Kento couldn't work out. A Sampler's curves come in too.
  • EdgeDetectWrapper keeps its erode size, so a blur set from it works. The erode itself isn't in Kento yet.
  • Of the studio library's 23 gizmos, 18 now work and the other 5 have some controls that do nothing yet. None fails. Across the studio's 225 latest comps, the knobs Kento can't work out went from 595 to about 440.

Kento Alpha 0.9.32, build 2860

Fixes

  • Kento no longer crashes viewing a chain of deep nodes, such as a DeepFromImage fed a deep picture.
  • A comp file that won't open no longer closes Kento when you open it from Finder or start Kento with it. Kento opens on an empty comp and says why, and File > Open says why too. Before, the reason was only in the log.
  • Saving a comp with animation, or with a Tracker's linked Transform, no longer warns that the animation or the link wasn't kept. Both were always kept.
  • Rendering a Write with no file says so ("WriteSmoke has no file: set where it writes first") before the render is queued. Before, every frame failed with a Python error.
  • The Node Graph draws no circles for knob expressions, as Nuke draws none. A Tracker's linked export and an imported comp's expressions were green circles with a wire to every knob they drove. The link lines show what reads what.
  • A panel has no two tabs of the same name: Reformat showed Reformat twice, and LensDistortion showed LensDistortion twice.
  • A channels menu names the channels its switches show. Erode's read "none...lpha".
  • The Tracker panel's planar track row fits the panel: its last switch, points on it, ran off the edge.
  • Two false errors are gone from the log: one for a frame stopped part way, one for the Viewer's view menu after a workspace change.
  • A Nuke control Kento doesn't need, such as Profile's open profile panel, no longer takes a dim row on the panel. Its tip in the Node Reference says why.

New

  • Viewer > Ignore pixel aspect shows an anamorphic picture as its pixels are stored, square. The pixels themselves are untouched.
  • Profile's Profile... button opens a window that times each node above it over the Profile's frames, slowest first, with each one's share.
  • PositionMatte's Pick in the Viewer sets its center from a click on the picture.
  • VectorCornerPin's Bake Corners keys its corners over the comp's frame range, where the vectors carry them.
  • CleanPlate fills in steps, finer to coarser, and takes a garbage matte. It matches Nuke's.
  • MatchGrade has a mask and a mix, and apply to mask applies the match only inside the mask, as in Nuke.
  • The Node Reference lists each node's panel buttons and what they do.
  • Kento's remote control tells an assistant what changed since it last asked (comps opened and closed, the frame, the selection, nodes made and deleted). Nodes it makes go under their input or beside the graph, not on top of each other. Its saves are Kento's own; they wrote a file Kento couldn't open.

Nuke scripts

  • Nuke's built-in layers are named channel sets: motion (forward and backward), disparity, mask, rotopaint_mask, the planar and spline-warp masks, sample, cutout and deep. AddChannels with any of them stopped the render.
